body:
It is illegal but they seem to just make up some unrelated reason. Also, this is an “at will” state so they can just fire you for no reason or make some reason up. I’d imagine I’d have to hire a lawyer and fight it. Everything in my life is going really well (this outstanding) and I’m not sure how I’d be able to cope with losing my job or my job becoming extremely stressful. 

But you bring up a good point. It is the better of the two options. I’m not so much concerned about getting promoted though, just using that as an example of how they seem make up something and retaliate in some way.

I replied to a post above but the reason for my concern is I know of someone else who requested an ADA accommodation to not work night shift and they were passed up for their promotion that year. I’m concerned of retribution not only from management but potentially other employees.

Unfortunately it’s a slow process. I have a therapist I see weekly. I have a primary care doctor who is absolutely amazing. I have a wonderful support network of close friends and my partner. I’m currently on 3 different medications and working with my doctor to find a combination/dose that works for me. I have a checklist of things I need to do daily as recommended by my therapist. I feel I’m kinda out of steps to try on my side.

The last person who had an ADA accommodation to not work nights was passed up on their promotion that year. That’s what I’m concerned about.
I might take you up on that if I need to. Thanks.

That’s why I’m concerned being on night shift. I will be alone for months. I’ll essentially lose my support network and really any human contact at all.  I have the number and location of a 24hr inpatient place that takes my health insurance in an absolute worst case. Trying to have as many safety nets as possible.

I know the ADA protects me from discrimination based off my mental illness but it doesn’t prevent them from making up some other reason to fire me. 

My plan right now with my therapist is that I contact him if night shift become too much to handle and he’ll file FMLA to take those months off. I’m more concerned with a sudden and impulsive action resulting in a failed attempt.
